userPrompt:
When a reply was misread, someone can overrule that verdict. The spec has
nothing yet on changing a task's outcome after it ends, so this is new.

When this is done:
- A task judged failed from its reply shows "Mark as done" beside its reason. A task judged done shows "Mark as failed" in the menu of its output.
- Either choice sets the status (spec/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.pi#MessageList.status) and saves it with the task's record, so it survives a restart.
- Its tooltip says the outcome was set by hand.
- A chain stopped by the overruled step offers to send the steps it didn't run.
- A story whose task is overruled to Done goes to Done when the sprint is closed (spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint). One overruled to Failed goes back to Next sprint.
- Only a task that has ended can be overruled. A task that failed to compile or run, or that the harness reported as an error, offers neither choice.
systemPrompt:
We're working in a project whose spec is compiled to .claude/reference, which is where to read it. Each prompt starts with a <task-instructions> block saying what that prompt is for and what it may change. Follow the block at the top of the prompt you are answering; an earlier prompt's block no longer applies.

Its code is located in ./src.

Its spec's Piton source, in ./spec, is only where edits to the spec go.

Read the spec from its compiled reference under .claude/reference, where inheritance, expressions, and links are already resolved, or, for one thing, from what `piton slice` prints for it with this harness's adapter.

Never read the .pi source under ./spec to learn what the spec says; that is only where edits to the spec go.

Read only what the change depends on, and start the work as soon as you have. Links to .claude/reference/... in the prompt are the spec for what they name: read those, and then only the pages they link to that the change actually depends on. Don't survey the spec, list its folders, or search it before you start. A page the prompt already gives you as a slice is already read: never read it again. Don't re-read anything you've already read.
instructions:
We're working on the code, located in ./src. Change the code so it does what the prompt asks, as the spec describes it.

When the work is about Suspense, its modes, its prompts, or its questions, or you are to write a prompt or a question for the user, first read .suspense/suspense-fluency.md once in this conversation, unless you already have: it is how Suspense works.

The spec's Piton source is in ./spec. Don't change it, and don't read it to learn what the spec says: read the compiled reference instead, as above. If the prompt asks for something the spec doesn't describe, or describes differently, say so in your reply rather than working around it.

Once you have read what the change depends on, and before your first change, write the constraints this task must meet to .suspense/history/1791887724-MarkATaskFailedWhenItsReplySaysItFailed3.understanding.md, once. Rewrite it only when a constraint in it turns out to be wrong, never after each page you read. It is a Markdown list and nothing else: one line per constraint, at most twelve, each a single short, specific statement of what must be true, written as a link to the compiled reference file it comes from, such as `- [The chain tab has no bottom border in combined mode](.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chain)`. Only list what the spec says; leave out anything you are deciding yourself. Replace a constraint when you learn it was wrong rather than adding another.

End with a reply of a few sentences saying what changed, or for a question, the answer, not a recap of the work or of what you read.

This prompt is the second step of a chain. Its first step changed the spec to meet it, and the spec has been built since. Now change the code so it does what the spec now says, without changing the spec. Follow the spec the prompt references, and the anchors the spec step names below. Where the spec and the prompt disagree, follow the spec, and say so in your reply.

The code is located in ./src.

The spec's source, which this step doesn't change, is in ./spec.

The prompt the chain was sent:

A task whose run ends without a harness error, but whose reply says it
couldn't do the work, is recorded and shown as Failed, never as Done.
That covers a reply saying it failed, that it couldn't write or change
the code, that it was blocked by the sandbox or by a missing file, or
that it gave up. Today a task finishes in the state of its last
result, as spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi#HarnessIntegration.feeding
says, so any such reply reads Done. The spec has nothing yet on judging
a run by what its reply says, so this is new.

Have the run report whether it did the work in a form the application
can read reliably. For example, the mode system prompts could ask every
task to end its reply with a fixed verdict line, and the application
would read that line, rather than guessing from the wording of free
text. A reply that gives no verdict keeps today's behaviour. Where the
verdict says it failed, the task takes the "Failed" label from
spec/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/Status.pi#MessageListStatus.description.
Its output says why, in the run's own words, as
spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi#HarnessIntegration.failures
asks of every failed run, and it is saved as Failed in its history
record, so it reads the same after a restart.

Since it is Failed, everything that already follows a failed task
follows it. In a chain, the next step is never sent and the chain reads
Failed, as spec/scope/prompt-mode/index.pi#PromptEditor.chainedTasks
says. In Planning, the story's card shows Failed, as
spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.states says. The story never
counts as Done, and Close sprint sends it back to the start of Next
sprint rather than into Done, as spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint
says. Start automatically doesn't start the next sprint because of it,
as spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.autoStart says.

Write this into the spec first, in HarnessIntegration's feeding or
failures and wherever the verdict is asked for, then make the code
match it.

What the spec step said it changed, its final output:

A task whose reply ends with `SUSPENSE-VERDICT: failed` now finishes Failed, even when the harness reported success. But the app won't build until you create one file I couldn't write: this sandbox has no write access to `.suspense/system-prompts/`.

**Create `.suspense/system-prompts/task-verdict.md`** with the text from `ModeSystemPrompts.verdict`:

```
After your reply, end with one line of its own that is exactly `SUSPENSE-VERDICT: done` if you did the work this prompt asks for, or exactly `SUSPENSE-VERDICT: failed` if you couldn't: if you failed, couldn't write or change what you were to, were blocked by the sandbox, a missing file, or anything else, or gave up. When it is failed, say in your reply, before that line, what stopped you. Write nothing after that line.
```

The code bakes it in through `system_prompts::task_verdict()`. For the same reason, the shipped `.suspense/system-prompts/suspense-fluency.md` still doesn't say that prompts never include the verdict line. That sentence needs adding by hand.

**What changed:**
- **The request:** Code, Chain and Spec tasks, including a chain's code step and a Code task sent to Spec, now get the verdict request last in their instructions. Questions, resume messages and Freeform don't (`src/hidden_anchor.rs`).
- **Reading it:** the app reads only the last non-blank line of the last result's reply, trimmed and ignoring case. It takes that line out of the reply, so it is never shown or handed to the next step (`src/task_table.rs`).
- **Failing the task:** if the line says failed, the task is marked Failed and its reply appears under the heading "The run reported that it couldn't do the work." (`src/prompt_mode.rs`).
- **After a restart:** the history replays the run's saved output, so the task still reads Failed.
- **Downstream:** chains and Planning already handle Failed tasks, so they follow without further changes.

**Testing:** I couldn't build in place. The other baked prompts and the project config can't be read from here either, so I type-checked and tested a copy of the crate using placeholder prompt files. It compiles, and the new `a_failed_verdict_fails_the_task` test passes. I updated the existing instruction tests for the verdict, but in that copy they fail on setup, before reaching what changed, so they haven't actually run. Please run the suite once the file exists.
